description: Small hosting and deploy tools (Railway, Render, Serverless, Ansible playbooks and ad-hoc commands) and Twilio. Google Cloud, Azure, Fly.io, Heroku, Firebase, Wrangler, and Stripe have their own packs.

rules.note: `serverless print` prints the configuration with its variables resolved, such as `${env:API_KEY}` and `${ssm:...}`, so it prints secrets (dev round 3).
Deployments, scaling, secrets, and removal on a hosting platform.
Serverless and Ansible playbooks deploy or change servers. The Ansible check mode (`--check`), `--syntax-check`, and the `--list-*` options only show what the playbook would do.
`railway variables` prints the values of the environment variables, unless the command sets or deletes one. `railway connect` opens a database shell with the credentials of the service.
`railway down` removes the latest deployment of the service. `railway delete` removes a project.
`ansible-vault view` prints decrypted secrets. `decrypt` writes them to the file as plain text. `edit` opens them in an editor.
`ansible-galaxy install` downloads roles or collections from outside the project.
An ad-hoc Ansible command runs a module or a shell command on remote hosts. `-m ping` and `-m setup` only check and read.

From `-vvv` on, Ansible prints the arguments of each module call, such as a password or a token from an environment lookup, unless the task or the module hides them (`no_log`). `-vvvv` adds the connection debug output (dev round 4).

safe.note: The linked project and environment, logs, the account, and project listings. `railway domain` makes a new domain, and `environment new` makes an environment, so they are not here (dev round 3).

The ping module, syntax checks, and listings of hosts and tasks do not change a host. The fact module (`setup`) prints the environment of the remote user (`ansible_env`), which can hold secrets, so it is not here (dev round 3).
